brief.subject: Dementia and gun safety; what the midterms mean for Medicare
brief.headline: Gun Safety When Dementia Appears, and the Medicare Debate After the Midterms
brief.dek: Experts look at firearm safety for older gun owners with memory decline, and why a new Congress may not bring Medicare for All.
brief.lede: Public health experts are developing ways to promote firearm safety among older gun owners, especially those showing signs of cognitive decline.

sections.heading: Firearms and early dementia
bullets: Public health experts are working on approaches to encourage safe gun practices among older adults who own firearms.
Signs of cognitive decline are a key focus, a concern for families caring for a gun-owning parent or spouse.
Families with questions about a loved one's memory changes should talk with that person's doctor.

sections.heading: Midterms reshape the Medicare debate
bullets: Democrats won control of Congress in the midterms, helped by voter frustration over healthcare costs.
Democratic control does not guarantee Medicare for All, despite hopes from some supporters.
Older adults on Medicare should watch for debate over any changes, though no specific proposals are reported.

brief.seo_description: Firearm safety for older gun owners with signs of dementia, plus what the Democratic midterm win may mean for Medicare for All.

items.title: When a Gun Owner Shows Early Signs of Dementia
items.snippet: Public health experts are finding ways to encourage firearm safety practices for older adults who own guns, especially when there are indications of cognitive decline.

items.title: Midterm Wave Sets a Course for ‘Medicare for All’ Fight
items.snippet: Voter frustration with healthcare costs helped fuel the Democrats’ midterm takeover of Congress. But Democratic control doesn’t mean “Medicare for All” will follow, as some hoped.
